paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the training loss over time for two models: “Vanilla” (a standard Transformer) and “SepLLM” (the proposed model), with the goal of comparing their convergence behavior under identical training conditions. The x-axis, labeled “Training Time (s)”, spans from 0 to 250,000 seconds on a linear scale, with major tick marks at intervals of 50,000 seconds. The y-axis, labeled “Loss”, ranges from 2.40 to 2.75, also on a linear scale, with major ticks every 0.05 units. The “Vanilla” model is represented by a purple line with downward-pointing triangle markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 2.75 loss at 0 seconds and steadily declines to about 2.50 loss by 250,000 seconds. The “SepLLM” model is shown as a red line with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts slightly lower than Vanilla at around 2.72 loss and decreases more steeply, reaching approximately 2.49 loss by 250,000 seconds. A green dashed horizontal line at 2.50 loss and vertical dashed lines at 200,000 and 250,000 seconds frame a highlighted region labeled “1.26×”, indicating that SepLLM reaches a comparable loss level to Vanilla approximately 1.26 times faster. Both lines exhibit smooth, monotonic decreases, with SepLLM consistently maintaining a lower loss than Vanilla across the entire training duration.
